**Scope:** Each row records the live status of a `STORY-*` row from `backlog.yaml` / `08-product-backlog.md` as proven by the current `ui-design-prototype/` tree. This file is **derived** — regenerated by `tools/coverage.mjs` and human-edited only when the regenerator disagrees with reality.

**Source of truth for initial status:** the three audits in `docs/planning/research/build-vs-plan-2026-09-06/` (`patient-ui-audit.md`, `admin-ui-audit.md`, `cross-cutting-audit.md`).

> Live prototype status: see this file for the current Done / Partial / Missing rollup.

## Proof citation convention

Write a proof as `` `path/to/file.js:1234 anchorText` `` — a **full** repo-relative
path, the line, and an **anchor**: a string that literally appears on that line
(a function name, an `id="..."`, a `data-*` attribute, a `// STORY-XYZ` marker).

The anchor is the source of truth. The line number is derived, and
`tools/proof-check.mjs` maintains it:

```
node tools/proof-check.mjs          # verify — non-zero exit on a broken citation
node tools/proof-check.mjs --fix    # re-resolve drifted line numbers in place
```

Why: line numbers rot the instant anyone inserts code above them, and
`coverage.mjs` only checks that the *file* exists — so a row can cite a
confidently wrong line forever. When this convention was introduced, 21 of the
then-current citations had already drifted (one by 634 lines) and nothing had
noticed. A citation without an anchor is reported as unverifiable; prefer the
`// STORY-XYZ:` markers already used throughout `ui-design-prototype/`.

## Status legend

- **Done** — the proof point is visible in the running prototype and matches the story contract. Closing `Closes STORY-XYZ` is appropriate when the PR lands.
- **Partial** — at least one required surface exists in the prototype, but one or more acceptance criteria are missing or stubbed. Closing the story would overstate coverage.
- **Missing** — no patient- or admin-facing proof in the prototype. Story is in the backlog but the prototype has not touched it yet.
- **Blocked** — work exists but cannot land without an external decision (legal, third-party, scope). Not used in this initial population.
- **Won't Do** — deliberately descoped from this prototype (e.g. R3 epics before R3 starts). Not used in this initial population.

Together they enforce WCAG AA — 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text — on every interactive surface across the admin console and the patient app, in both colour schemes. Bug class closed on 2026-09-10: 20 admin hover states were below AA because `--surface-hover` resolved to `--accent-soft` (a 10%-alpha fill, not a text-grade surface); remapping to `--fill-secondary` (= `--glass-2`) brings `--ink` on the hover background above the AA threshold in both schemes. Detector + probe are both wired into `npm run check` and skip cleanly when chromium or the dev server is absent. (Annotation form: `STORY-NFR-AA-HOVER-001`.) |
